title: Curd Rice (Thayir Sadam)
tagline: Cooling, creamy yoghurt rice with a fragrant tempering — comfort in a bowl.
intro: Curd rice, or thayir sadam, is the soothing finale to a South Indian meal — soft rice folded into fresh yoghurt with a fragrant tempering of mustard, curry leaves and ginger. Cooling, gentle on the stomach and quietly delicious, it's the ultimate comfort food, especially in hot weather.

items: 2 cups cooked rice, slightly mashed while warm
2 tbsp pomegranate seeds or grated carrot

method: Mash the warm cooked rice lightly and let it cool a little.
Stir in the yoghurt, milk and salt to a soft, creamy consistency.
For the tempering, heat oil and pop the mustard seeds; add urad dal, green chillies, ginger, red chilli, curry leaves and asafoetida, and fry until fragrant.
Pour the tempering over the curd rice and mix.
Fold in any add-ins and garnish with coriander. Serve slightly chilled or at room temperature.
tips: Add the yoghurt when the rice is warm (not hot) so it stays creamy, not split.
A splash of milk keeps it soft if it's made ahead and thickens.
toServe: Delicious with mango or lime pickle.
imageAlt: Curd rice with tempering of mustard seeds and curry leaves
